note: The one list of what this product ships that somebody else wrote.
Read by four things, which is why it exists: scripts/make-third-party-notices.py
writes THIRD-PARTY-LICENCES from it, scripts/check-third-party-notices.py holds
ui/src/about.cpp and the two READMEs' tables to agreeing with it, and the
packaging scripts install the result. Before this file the same list was kept in
two places by hand and about.cpp's own comment admitted it; the two had drifted
by five components, LAME among them, whose licence asks in as many words to be
`licences` names files in third_party/licences/, carried verbatim from the
component's own tree or, for the long canonical texts, from the Free Software
Foundation's and the Apache Software Foundation's own wording. An empty
`licences` means the text travels from the machine the package is built on,
which is where that library comes from: see `third-party/` in the staged tree.
`notice` is what a recipient is shown; `offered` and `verdict` are the argument,
and the argument is longer in README.md than a user wants on a screen.
